title: Azure SDK for .NET
description: Install Azure SDK packages in an ASP.NET Core project and make your first Azure SDK call.

data.text: The Azure SDK for .NET is distributed as NuGet packages. Each Azure service has its own package, and they follow common conventions for authentication, retries, and async APIs.

data.title: Install Azure Blob Storage and Key Vault packages
data.content: Use the dotnet CLI or Package Manager Console to add Azure SDK packages.
data.code:
dotnet add package Azure.Storage.Blobs
dotnet add package Azure.Security.KeyVault.Secrets
dotnet add package Azure.Identity

data.text: `DefaultAzureCredential` is the recommended way to authenticate. It automatically chains multiple credential types together: environment variables, managed identity, Visual Studio login, Azure CLI login, and more.

data.title: Authenticate with DefaultAzureCredential
data.content: This single class works locally and in Azure without code changes.

data.title: Local development flow
data.text: When running locally, `DefaultAzureCredential` uses `AzureCliCredential` behind the scenes if you are already logged in with `az login`. When deployed to Azure, it can use a managed identity automatically.
Create a Reusable Azure Client Factory
In ASP.NET Core, register Azure clients in `Program.cs` so they are available through dependency injection.

data.title: Register Azure clients in Program.cs
data.content: Use the Azure SDK extensions to register typed clients for DI.

data.title: Add Azure SDK to a web app
data.description: Create a new ASP.NET Core app and add the Azure SDK packages.
steps: Run the `dotnet add package` commands shown above
Run the app and verify it starts without errors
data.expectedOutcome: The app starts successfully and the Azure clients are registered in the DI container.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure SDK packages are distributed through NuGet
`DefaultAzureCredential` removes the need for hardcoded connection strings
`AddAzureClients` in ASP.NET Core centralizes Azure client registration
Prefer `async` APIs for all Azure service calls
data.takeaway: Once the SDK packages and credential strategy are in place, the rest of the course focuses on using individual Azure services from C#.
